key_insight: Realistic piezoelectrically actuated wall deformations can substantially reduce turbulent skin-friction drag, with spanwise waves delivering the strongest effect.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical active-surface strategy for flow control in channels, pipes, and other wall-bounded turbulent systems where drag reduction can lower energy use.
method: Performed DNS of turbulent half-channel flow at Reτ = 200 over prescribed moving-wall deformations.
Modeled piezoelectric actuation with finite-element analysis across 119–543 Hz and 250–500 V to obtain realistic wall-wave shapes.
Tested upstream, downstream, and spanwise deformation directions, including travelling, hybrid, and standing waves.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports maximum drag reductions of 1.6% for upstream waves, 5.4% for downstream waves, and 27.6% for spanwise waves.
watch_item: The strongest drag reduction is shown at moderate Reynolds number and with idealized simulation-based actuation, so hardware durability, power cost, and performance at higher-Re flows remain key concerns.
paper_title: Direct numerical simulations of turbulent drag reduction via piezoelectric actuation
